message.content: One of the most celebrated works of the 19th‑century sculpture canon is **Auguste Rodin’s “Le Penseur” (“The Thinker”)**. Although Rodin began modeling it in the late 1800s and the bronze cast that is now world‑famous was produced in 1902–03, the original marble version was first exhibited in 1880 and the concept dates back to 1881. Its dramatic pose, psychological depth, and technical mastery made it emblematic of the era’s shift toward expressive realism and earned it a place among the most recognizable sculptures worldwide.
